title: Three Callers
summary: Three computers keep calling the same outside address like clockwork. Two of them are doing their job. One is checking in with someone who shouldn't be there.
story: You are the analyst on shift at {{CO}} (a made-up company). A new rule looks for 'beaconing': a computer connecting to the same outside address at regular intervals, the way a hidden program checks in for orders. On its first day it fired on three computers. Lots of honest software does the same.
goal: Find the one computer that is really infected, the program, the address it calls, how often, the account and when it began.
skills: beaconing, regular connections, network events per program, telling honest background software from a hidden program

questions.ask: The beaconing alert on WS-{{HA}}: real attack or false alarm? (one try)
questions.explain: {{TIMEH}} syncs its clock with ntp.clockwork.example (the time service, port 123) and {{UPDH}} asks wu.osvendor.example for updates, both through svchost.exe. {{BADH}} connects to a bare address on port 443 from rundll32.exe, loading a DLL from a user's Temp folder.
The one whose connections come from rundll32.exe and go to an address no name lookup explains.
image= on the network events (event=3) for that address.

questions.ask: How many seconds apart are its calls?
questions.explain: The difference between the times of one call and the next.

questions.ask: Which account is it running as?
At what time (HH:MM:SS) did it first call that address?

hints.text: Regular isn't the same as bad. For each computer, ask which program connects, to which name (is there a DNS lookup for that address?) and on which port. Process events with event=3 record network connections per program.
